# Model overview

The **Non-Elective Flow Simulation** is an open-source discrete-event simulation developed by Helena Robinson at Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust. It represents patients moving from the emergency department into SDEC or an inpatient bed and explores how bed capacity, admitted length of stay and SDEC activity affect queues and waiting times. The model is written in Python using SimPy and includes a Streamlit interface.

[How to join](../../join-us/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .session-join-action}

{{< include ../_all-sessions.qmd >}}

## Actions for participants before the session

- Attempt to reproduce the model by using GitHub Codespaces (recommended for participants new to GitHub; see the [repository README](https://github.com/ReModel-Club/Non-Elective-Flow-Simulation#readme) for instructions) or by cloning the repository and running it locally.
- Try the browser-based [Streamlit application](https://non-elective-flow-simulation-coch.streamlit.app/).
- Explore the repository and its structure.

::: {.callout-warning title="Local software requirement"}
**This model uses Python.** To run it locally, you will need Python installed and will need to install the packages specified by the repository. You can use the hosted Streamlit application without installing Python.
:::

## Getting help

If you have a problem running or reusing the Non-Elective Flow Simulation, [open an issue in the ReModel repository](https://github.com/ReModel-Club/Non-Elective-Flow-Simulation/issues). This is the best way to contact the ReModel team about the model. Describe what you were trying to do, what happened and any error messages you received.

## Session objectives and outline

This will be a discussion session around the model and our attempts to run the model as it currently exists. Participants will discuss:

- any issues they had in running the model in its current form;
- any areas of the model they didn't understand;
- how we think the model is structured from inputs through to outputs;
- how patients, queues, resources and events are represented;
- assumptions for arrivals, length of stay, capacity and SDEC activity;
- where they think this model might be useful.

The aim is for participants to leave this session with a clear understanding of how to run the model and a working version of the model that they can continue to explore before the Reuse session.
